quotes.text: Power automate owns the logic. This isn't a limitation of the tool. It is a core design principle.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the central architectural split of the episode in three short sentences.

quotes.text: If you are running a process where the output must be identical every time, like a financial calculation or a compliance check, you do not want an agent making that call.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete rule for when not to use an AI agent.

quotes.text: A flow fails at the step where the error occurred and stops, but an agent fails and asks what to do next.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorably contrasts deterministic flows with adaptive agents.

quotes.text: Governance for agents is a design discipline, not an audit function or a post-built review. You have to embed it into the architecture from the very first conversation about what the agent is supposed to do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes agent governance as an architectural responsibility rather than a compliance checklist.

quotes.text: The platform can generate the artifacts, but it cannot replace judgment. It can't decide which layer should own a specific decision
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Answers the episode's title question about which part of low-code work remains irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Why the low-code model is breaking
Copilot Studio is not a chatbot
Governance as the new core skill

takeaways: Copilot Studio agents should own judgment while Power Automate flows own deterministic logic, with a clean line between the two layers.
Canvas apps break at scale because business logic lives on screens, but they still win for structured forms, offline work, device integration and dense data grids.
Low-code developers stay relevant by moving into logic architecture: data governance, evaluation, human-in-the-loop design, integration depth and AI risk management.
hook: Microsoft has moved its center of investment from canvas apps to Copilot Studio and agents, and many Power Platform makers are still building on the old foundation. This episode is for low-code developers and architects who want to understand the new split between agent judgment and flow logic, the governance and security implications, and the concrete steps to grow into a logic architect role.
